answer: At the summit of security measures, an agent economy can enforce a unique work trail for each identity. To prevent sybil attacks, the system anchors each new identity to a previous one, requiring a continuous chain of work. If an attacker tries to create multiple identities, the system will detect the divergence and flag it, preventing them from making the system wander into insecure territory, as each new identity must build on the previous one, making it costly for the attacker to create and maintain multiple fake identities.
